content.text:
Fixed: `qs.stringify` now encodes a lone surrogate as `%EF%BF%BD` (U+FFFD) and keeps the next character. The full suite passes (1241 tests).

**Cause:** in `encode` (`lib/utils.js`), any surrogate code unit was assumed to be the first half of a pair. It always consumed the next code unit and merged the two, even when that unit wasn't a low surrogate. That is how the `x` or the space got swallowed.

**Fix:** a surrogate now only combines with the next unit when it is a high surrogate (D800–DBFF) followed by a low surrogate (DC00–DFFF). Otherwise it is emitted as `%EF%BF%BD` and the next character is processed on its own. Valid pairs encode as before.

I ran your examples:
- `'\uD800x'` gives `a=%EF%BF%BDx`.
- `'x\uDBFF'` gives `a=x%EF%BF%BD`.
- `'\uDC00 '` gives `a=%EF%BF%BD%20`.
- `'😀'` still gives `%F0%9F%98%80`.

Two existing tests in `test/utils.js` asserted the old buggy output (the swallowed character and the garbage bytes). I changed their expected values to the new behaviour:
- **Chunk boundary:** the lone-surrogate-at-a-chunk-boundary test now expects `%EF%BF%BDX`.
- **`encodes lone surrogates`:** it now expects `%EF%BF%BD%20%EF%BF%BD`.

I didn't add new test cases beyond those two edits.
